name: ui/device-code
title: DeviceCode
summary: The device side of OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization (RFC 8628 §3.3): the user code large and monospace, the short verification address, a QR code of the complete address drawn on the device, an expiry countdown and a live status line. For pairing a TV, display or desktop app from a phone. One contract for the Astro, React and Mzizi Roots builds.

divergences: Takes `onRefresh` (called when the refresh control is pressed) beside `refreshHref`; the Astro build dispatches a bubbling `device-code:refresh` event instead.
`expiresAt` and `now` are Unix milliseconds (`i64`); `rfc3339_to_unix_ms` reads an RFC 3339 string. Takes `on_refresh` (an `EventHandler<MouseEvent>`) beside `refresh_href`.
Renders one frame: the app re-renders it each second with a new `now` to tick the countdown.

props.name: userCode
props.description: RFC 8628 `user_code`. Shown upper case, letters and digits only, in groups of four (`KTQB-4RMX`).

props.name: verificationUri
props.description: RFC 8628 `verification_uri`: the short address a person types on their phone. Shown without its scheme.

props.name: verificationUriComplete
props.description: RFC 8628 `verification_uri_complete`: the address with the code in it, drawn as the QR code (byte mode, error correction M) on the device, never by a network service.

props.name: expiresAt
props.description: When the code lapses: an ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 string, Unix milliseconds or a Date. Compute it on the device from `expires_in` when the code arrives.

props.name: status
props.description: Where the pairing stands, from polling the token endpoint: `authorization_pending` and `slow_down` are pending, `access_denied` is denied, `expired_token` is expired, a token is approved. A pending code past `expiresAt` shows as expired.

props.name: size
props.description: phone for a hand-held or windowed screen; tv for a screen read from across a room (a 10-foot UI): larger code, address, QR code and controls.

props.name: now
props.description: The clock for the server render (and for tests). The current time when omitted; the enhancement ticks from the device's clock.

props.name: refreshHref
props.description: Makes the refresh control a link to this address, which works with no script. Without it the control is a button.

props.name: class
props.description: Extra classes on the root, merged last.

behaviour: The root is a group named "Link this device" with `data-status` (the status shown) and `data-size`, and `data-expires-at` in Unix milliseconds.

While pending it shows, in order: "On your phone, go to", the address without its scheme, "and enter this code", the user code in a box bordered with the brand's primary colour, "Expires in m:ss", and the QR code of `verificationUriComplete` with a caption.
The user code is formatted from whatever the server sent: upper case, letters and digits only, in groups of four joined by a hyphen.
The countdown rounds up to the second. With one minute or less left the status line says "Less than a minute left to enter the code."
A pending code past `expiresAt` shows as expired: the code, address and QR code are removed, and the status line and refresh control show.
approved shows "This device is linked."; expired, denied and error show their message and a "Get a new code" control; denied and error colour the message with the destructive token.

The refresh control is a link when `refreshHref` is given, otherwise a button. React calls `onRefresh`; Rust calls `on_refresh`; the Astro enhancement dispatches a bubbling `device-code:refresh` CustomEvent on the root.
While pending, the refresh control is rendered `hidden`, so the enhancement can show it the moment the code lapses without a round trip.
The QR code is dark modules on white with a four-module quiet zone in both themes, drawn as one SVG path in `currentColor`: no image, no network request, no inline style.

lapsed.description: Still pending on the server, but past its expiry.

refresh-link.description: Expired, with a link to start again (works with no script).

roles: img (the QR code, named "QR code for <address>")
timer (the time left; not announced each second)
status (the status line, a polite live region)
keyboard: The refresh control is the only interactive element: a native button or link, reached with Tab, or with a TV remote's arrows and OK where the platform maps them to focus and Enter.
focus: A visible focus ring in the ring token on the refresh control (8px on tv, for a screen across a room).
aria: The visible code is aria-hidden; a screen-reader-only line reads it one character at a time with a pause between groups ("Code: K T Q B, 4 R M X"), so it is never read as a word.
The QR code is role=img with an aria-label naming the full address, so the address is available without the image.
Status changes (approved, expired, declined, an error, the last minute) are announced through the role=status line; the countdown itself is a timer, which is not live.
The pending dot is decorative (aria-hidden) and pulses only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference (motion-safe:). Nothing else moves.

theming.brandOverlay: --primary (the code's border, the pending dot and the refresh control) and --ring: Mukoko's tanzanite under the Mukoko overlay. The QR code is black on white in every theme and brand, because cameras read dark-on-light most reliably.

noJs.without: Everything renders from the server's clock: the code, address, QR code, the time left when the page was made, the status and, with `refreshHref`, a working refresh link.
noJs.with: The countdown ticks each second from the device's clock, the last minute is announced, a lapsed code turns to expired with its refresh control, and the refresh button dispatches `device-code:refresh`.

responsive: From 320px: one centred column (steps and code, then the QR code); the code never wraps and the address breaks anywhere.
phone caps the width at max-w-sm.
tv puts the steps and the QR code side by side from md up, with a 7xl code and a 320px QR code.
contract:
contract
  slot is "device-code"
  portal is "https://mzizi.dev/components/device-code"
  role is "group"
  label is "Link this device"
  class contains "bg-card"
  when default shows p "KTQB-4RMX"
  when default shows p "mukoko.com/link"
  when default shows span "9:42"
  when default shows span "Waiting for approval on your phone."
  when tv class contains "p-10"
  when last-minute shows span "Less than a minute left to enter the code."
  when lapsed shows button "Get a new code"
  when expired shows span "This code has expired."
  when expired shows button "Get a new code"
  when refresh-link shows a "Get a new code"
  when approved shows span "This device is linked."
  when denied shows span "The request was declined."
  when error shows span "Something went wrong."
  button "Get a new code" min_height 48
end

checks.say: The root names the status and size it shows.
The tv size is named on the root.
The visible code is formatted in groups of four and hidden from screen readers.
The code is spelled out for screen readers, one character at a time.
checks.text: Code: K T Q B, 4 R M X

checks.say: The address is shown without its scheme.
The QR code is an image named with the full address.
The QR code is one path in currentColor.
The time left is a timer.
Every state has one polite status line.
While pending, the refresh control waits hidden.
A lapsed code shows as expired.
A lapsed code no longer shows its QR code.
An expired code is not shown.
Once ended, the refresh control is visible.
The refresh control is a button by default.
With refreshHref the refresh control is a link.
With refreshHref there is no button.
Approved has nothing to press and no code.

gaps: The copy is English only; a locale's words need a text prop or slot in a later minor version.
The Rust build does not tick on its own (no timer in a component library): the app re-renders it each second with a new `now`.
